# Derivation index {#sec-appb}

The derivation index helps a reader find the argument behind an update equation and the check associated with it. An indexed equation is a route to evidence, not evidence that the argument is correct or that its check has passed.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Find derivations and their associated checks.

**Data.** chapter Derivation layers; generated navigation tables.

**Placement.** Report preparation, outside the solver.

**Activation.** Run `gen_derivation_index.py`; no solver switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Index membership does not establish correctness.

**Evidence.** The checks below verify generation against its inputs.
:::

Local symbols: this guide introduces no mathematical variables. Symbols in the tables retain the definitions in their source chapters.

## Why the index is structured this way

1. Find the scheme and follow its equation link. `scheme_rows` emits one row per labelled equation in the Derivation layer; a layer with no label instead gets a prose row.
2. Read the statement in its chapter context. An entry in `tools/derivation-statements/chNN.json` overrides the automatically selected lead sentence, so the short statement is not the full derivation.
3. Follow the code citation from the chapter. The generator associates a nearby citation with the equation; proximity alone does not establish that every assumption is implemented.
4. Run the named check and read its claim. A script is listed when its name appears in the scheme and the file exists; that condition does not execute it. @sec-ch15 is deliberately excluded from the scheme census.

These operations parse strings and count rows with Python integers. They perform no floating-point reduction;
there is no accumulated round-off term to bound. Exact regeneration tests the rendering contract, not a physical tolerance.

## How to use and refresh the index

There is no simulation YAML for this appendix: neither generator configures snapy.
From the report directory (@sec-appa-refresh), run:

```bash
python tools/gen_derivation_index.py
python tools/gen_derivation_index.py --check
```

The first command regenerates the included table from its sources. The second refuses a stale committed fragment
with a nonzero exit status. Edit the inputs and regenerate; do not repair individual generated cells.
`--check` and `--stats` are mutually exclusive command-line modes. This is a report-tool refusal, not a solver guard.

The selection step in `gen_derivation_index.py` is:

```python
scripts = sorted({c for c in _CHECK.findall(whole)
                  if chk_dir and (chk_dir / c).exists()})
```

This excerpt implements step 4 above. It maps text to an index entry; there is no solver equation or timestep attached to it.
The generator implementation is part of the report revision, separate from the solver code pin.[^appb-source]

## Verification and limits

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gen_derivation_index.py --check` (report only) | Generated fragment agrees with current inputs | Exact text equality | Generator contract |
| `tools/tests/test_gen_derivation_index.py` (pytest, not CTest) | Parsing and index selection fixtures | Exact fixture assertions | Report-tool tests |

: Checks of the derivation index generator. {#tbl-appb-reader-checks}

[C1] A successful `--check` establishes that the table is current against its inputs.
It does not validate those inputs. [C2] The generator tests exercise the parsing and selection rules;
they do not execute a snapy simulation.[^appb-run]

The index does not verify algebra, code correspondence or check success. “Exists” classifies a reference to a derivation source; “re-derived” classifies its absence. Neither is a review verdict.

Printed floating-point residuals in the ch04 gnomonic, ch05 WB-reference, ch09 round-off and ch10 repair/kinetics checks
can differ in their last digits by host and library version. Compare each executable assertion against its stated
threshold; the committed outputs record one execution, not portable decimal constants.
